props.title: Jahmyr Gibbs OVER 29.5 receiving yards
props.cutoff: OVER 29.5 at -115 or better only; pass at 30.5+ or -116 and worse. Reverify the live price after expiry.
props.edge: Projected mean +3.5 yards, not a probability edge. Uncalibrated judgment: about 55% to clear, versus 53.49% break-even at -115 (about +1.5 percentage points; about +2.8% expected return if that estimate is right). Plausible 50–60% uncertainty includes negative value.
props.why: The verified 29.5-yard number is below his 34.4 last-five and 44.9 last-ten averages. Five targets and 30 receiving yards in Week 1 support continuing receiving involvement; the team confirms an expanded lead-back role. My conservative 33-yard projection uses 5.5 targets × 75% catches × 8 yards per catch, below the recent target averages. Buffalo favored by 5.5 gives a plausible passing script. Detroit line absences may encourage outlets, but that is an inference, not the main reason.
props.risk: Thin estimated edge and uncertain routes under a new coordinator. Missing Mahogany and Miller could require Gibbs to block instead. Buffalo held Houston RBs to four catches for 17 yards last week; that one game does not prove a favorable matchup. Overtime inflated Week 1 touches. Inactives and wind remain pregame checks; no unsupported weather or scheme boost.
